key_insight: Teach an AI what to draw before teaching it how to render. This paper separates visual generation into autoregressive pretraining for semantic knowledge and diffusion post-training for fine-grained image detail.
problem_solved: Visual generation needs both high-level understanding and precise pixel rendering. The paper investigates how to train for these complementary capabilities and which pretraining objective best supports later rendering.
method: Use autoregressive pretraining to acquire high-level semantic knowledge.
Apply diffusion post-training to learn high-fidelity rendering.
Study training objectives, representations, and scaling; controlled comparisons favor autoregression as the pretraining objective for downstream rendering.
impact: The approach offers practitioners a training strategy that assigns semantic learning and image rendering to different stages. The provided abstract is truncated, so specific performance gains and evaluation details are unavailable.
visual_elements: Two-stage pipeline: autoregressive knowledge acquisition → diffusion rendering → generated image.
Paired icons: a brain for semantic understanding and a paintbrush for pixel-level detail.

paper_title: Know, then Draw: A New Learning Paradigm for Visual Generation
paper_authors: Yucheng Mao, Chongjian Ge, Zhuowen Tu, Hao Tan, Hanwen Jiang
